sources.name: nats-server
sources.fips: Rebuilt with GOFIPS140=v1.0.0 and fips140=on by default: TLS (1.2+, approved suites only) and NKEY ed25519 signatures run in the Go Cryptographic Module v1.0.0. The binary also links golang.org/x/crypto, outside the module, for optional features the bundled configuration must not enable: bcrypt password hashes (use TLS client certificates or NKEYs), auth-callout xkey encryption (curve25519, chacha20poly1305, nacl) and blake2b; highwayhash is a non-cryptographic JetStream checksum.

sources.name: openbao
sources.fips: Rebuilt with GOFIPS140=v1.0.0, fips140=on by default, CGO_ENABLED=0 and without the ui tag. go-jose is raised to 4.1.6 for CVE-2026-116587 (fixed upstream after 2.6.6). The 2.6 line (security fixes released with 2.7.3 on 2026-11-19) is chosen because 2.7 requires Go 1.27. The barrier (AES-256-GCM), TLS (1.2+, approved suites), tokens and KV v2 run in the Go module. Outside it, for features the bundled configuration must not enable: PGP-wrapped unseal keys and root tokens (ProtonMail go-crypto, cloudflare/circl), the SSH secrets engine (x/crypto/ssh), Transit's chacha20-poly1305 and ed448 key types, PKCS#12 import. Without cgo the PKCS#11 seal is not built (OpenBao ships it only in its separate cgo 'hsm' build); cloud KMS and transit auto-unseal are.

sources.name: versitygw
sources.fips: Rebuilt with GOFIPS140=v1.0.0, fips140=on by default and CGO_ENABLED=0 (cgo is only in the rdma build tag): TLS (1.2+, approved suites: TLS 1.1 and ChaCha20 refused, checked 2026-11-26) and SigV4 (crypto/hmac with SHA-256) run in the Go module. MD5 is used for ETags and Content-MD5, not for security, as S3 defines them. Also linked, outside the module and unused by the bundled configuration (POSIX backend, --cert/--key): golang.org/x/crypto acme/autocert, pkcs12, md4 and blake2b (other backends and IAM integrations); xxh3 is a non-cryptographic checksum. Accounts: the internal IAM backend (--iam-dir on the data volume, users.json 0600) with role 'user' accounts that own one bucket each, checked 2026-11-26 (ADR-020).

sources.name: postgresql
sources.fips: Built --with-openssl against the libraries below; TLS, SCRAM-SHA-256, pgcrypto and its random numbers go through OpenSSL, so through the FIPS provider. PostgreSQL itself is not a validated module.

sources.name: openssl
sources.fips: The libraries (libssl, libcrypto) and the openssl command, LTS line; not validated themselves and built without enable-fips. They load the 3.1.2 FIPS provider, and openssl.cnf makes fips=yes the default property, so every algorithm is fetched from it.

sources.name: openssl-fips-provider
sources.fips: Validated: OpenSSL FIPS Provider 3.1.2, CMVP certificate #4985 (FIPS 140-3, sunset 2030-03-10), built from this tarball with enable-fips and installed by its own make install_fips (fipsinstall). The integrity check and the self-tests run at every load (-self_test_onload, the 3.1 default). Known FIPS-relevant CVEs fixed only in later, unvalidated 3.1.x releases: CVE-2024-13176 (ECDSA timing), CVE-2024-4603 and CVE-2023-6237 (slow public-key checks).

sources.name: keycloak
sources.fips: Keycloak's own image (Red Hat UBI 9, Red Hat OpenJDK 21), rebuilt with --features=fips --fips-mode=strict and the BC-FIPS jars below, as Keycloak's FIPS guide describes. Keycloak's cryptography runs in BC-FIPS in approved mode; the JVM itself is in FIPS mode (FIPS-JVM enabled) only on a FIPS-enabled RHEL-compatible node, which Keycloak requires for a supported FIPS deployment.

sources.name: bc-fips
sources.fips: The Bouncy Castle FIPS Java API (BC-FJA) on CMVP certificate #4943 (FIPS 140-3, interim validation, approved mode; sunset 2030-01-16), whose listed software version is 2.1.1. 2.1.3 is Bouncy Castle's patch release of that module (19 July 2026), described as under the certificate and in submission for listing; it is Keycloak 26.8.2's tested version and fixes CVE-2026-8763 (critical), CVE-2026-13505, CVE-2026-13506 and CVE-2026-8798 in 2.1.1. Run pure Java only (no native code): org.bouncycastle.native.cpu_variant=java.

sources.name: bctls-fips
sources.fips: Not a cryptographic module: the JSSE provider over bc-fips (Keycloak 26.8.2's version).

sources.name: bcpkix-fips
sources.fips: Not a cryptographic module: PKIX, CMS and certificate utilities over bc-fips (Keycloak 26.8.2's version).

sources.name: bcutil-fips
sources.fips: Not a cryptographic module: ASN.1 utilities over bc-fips (Keycloak 26.8.2's version).

sources.name: cloudnative-pg
sources.fips: Not rebuilt (D-OQ3): the operator does no data-path cryptography beyond its Kubernetes API client and the instance manager's TLS to PostgreSQL. Mirrored by digest after verifying the publisher's keyless signature (identity above, checked 2026-11-26), and re-signed with the release key; it joins deploy/third-party-images.json with the bundled manifests (T-08).
